SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints (onset coincides with starting new job; several weeks per patient):
  • Episodic frontal headaches at work (during laptop use/meetings); mild nausea associated; no radiation  
  • Reduced appetite with ~5 lb unintentional weight loss; no overt change in clothing fit  
  • Bilateral tingling “pins & needles” in both hands; no leg involvement  
  • Daily palpitations (heart “beating fast”) lasting seconds-minutes  
  • Intermittent shortness of breath while sitting at desk; none with exercise  
  • Decreased libido since job change
- Past Medical History: “Hyperthyroidism” (patient term) – currently treated with thyroxine.
- Medications: Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social History:
  • Occupation: Lawyer, high-stress environment (self-rated 7–8/10).  
  • Alcohol: ~2 glasses of wine once weekly.  
  • Tobacco: Denies.  
  • Recreational drugs: Denies.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during tele-visit.
- No vitals available.
- Planned investigations: thyroid function blood tests (per clinician).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headaches  
   - Assessment: New-onset episodic frontal headaches; likely tension/stress-related; rule out thyroid dysfunction or other secondary causes.  
   - Investigations planned: In-clinic physical exam; basic neuro exam; thyroid function tests (TFTs).  
   - Treatment planned: Await face-to-face review before initiating therapy.

2. Paresthesia in both hands  
   - Assessment: Bilateral hand tingling; etiology unclear (possible stress hyperventilation, neuropathy, thyroid disorder).  
   - Investigations planned: Neurological examination at in-person visit; consider further labs if indicated.

3. Palpitations / Intermittent tachycardia  
   - Assessment: Subjective palpitations; differential includes anxiety, thyroid dysfunction, arrhythmia.  
   - Investigations planned: Cardiovascular examination; consider ECG and TFTs at clinic visit.

4. Shortness of breath (at rest)  
   - Assessment: Episodic dyspnea while seated; no exertional component; could be anxiety/panic or thyroid related.  
   - Investigations planned: Respiratory and cardiovascular examination during visit.

5. Unintentional weight loss & reduced appetite  
   - Assessment: 5 lb loss; needs evaluation for thyroid status, stress, or other systemic illness.  
   - Investigations planned: TFTs; review diet and lifestyle at appointment.

6. Decreased libido  
   - Assessment: Onset concurrent with job stress; consider psychogenic vs endocrine (thyroid).  
   - Investigations planned: Address after TFTs and initial assessment.

Follow-up:
- Patient to book earliest available in-person appointment through clinic app.
- At visit: perform full physical exam (heart, lungs, neuro), vital signs, weight; order thyroid function panel and additional labs/ECG as clinically indicated.
- Patient advised no new medications until in-person review.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: vital signs, comprehensive allergies list, medication dose/frequency, full systems review.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” yet takes thyroxine (commonly prescribed for hypothyroidism) – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional fragmented sentences but clinically adequate.
